Spending a night at Maimuna's house, Ibn Abbas saw the Prophet pray four rak'at after Isha, sleep, then rise to pray, moving Ibn Abbas from his left to his right.
Staying at Maimuna's, Ibn Abbas saw the Prophet wake at midnight, recite the last ten verses of Al-Imran, make ablution and pray two rak'at six times and a witr.
Asked from the pulpit about night prayer, the Prophet said to pray two rak'at at a time and, fearing dawn, one rak'a as witr, the night's last prayer being odd.
People followed the Prophet's night prayer behind a low wall or mat; he stopped, fearing it would become compulsory, and said the best prayer is at home except the compulsory.
The Prophet praised Allah on rising for Tahajjud, prayed eleven rak'at with long prostrations, wished Ibn Umar prayed it after his dream of the Fire, and missed it when ill.
The Prophet urged the women of his dwellings, and Ali and Fatima, to pray at night, and left loved deeds like the mosque's Ramadan night prayer lest they become compulsory.
The Prophet prayed until his feet swelled, to be a thankful slave, rose at cock's crow, used siwak and stood long; David's prayer and fasting were most beloved to Allah.
The night prayer is two rak'at at a time ended by witr; the Prophet prayed seven to thirteen rak'at, and at night he could be seen praying or sleeping.
Satan's three knots on a sleeper are undone by remembrance, ablution and prayer; in a dream one who slept through prayers was punished, and Satan urinated in an oversleeper's ears.
The Prophet slept early and prayed late in the night, never over eleven rak'at in Ramadan or otherwise, his heart awake as his eyes slept, reciting sitting in old age.
The Prophet had a prayer rope removed and told people to pray while energetic, do deeds within their capacity, not abandon night prayer, and give body and family their right.
Whoever wakes at night, declares Allah's oneness and asks forgiveness is answered, his prayer after ablution accepted; Ibn Rawaha's verse says the Prophet spends nights away from his bed.
Staying at Maimuna's house, Ibn Abbas joined the Prophet's night prayer; the Prophet twisted his ear, prayed twelve rak'at in twos and one witr, then two light rak'at before Fajr.
Praying Ramadan nights in faith forgives past sins; Umar gathered the people behind one reciter; the Prophet stopped leading them lest it be made compulsory, and prayed eleven rak'at.
Staying with his aunt Maimuna, Ibn Abbas saw the Prophet wake at night, recite the last ten verses of Al Imran and pray two by two, ending with witr.
When the Prophet asked Ali and Fatima why they did not pray at night, Ali said they rise when Allah wills, and the Prophet recited that man is most quarrelsome.
The Prophet prayed at night until his feet swelled and cracked, though forgiven his past and future faults, wishing to be a thankful slave; when old he prayed sitting.
The Prophet rose in the last third of the night, looked at the sky reciting the verse on the creation of the heavens and earth, and prayed eleven rak'at.
